recipes.name: Chicken and Dumplings with Vegetables
ingredients_raw: 2 (10.75 ounce) cans condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Combine soup, water, chicken, celery, onion, salt, poultry seasoning, and pepper in a large, heavy pot. Cover and cook over low heat for 1 ½ hours.
Add potatoes and carrots; cover and cook for another 30 minutes.
Remove chicken from pot, shred it, and return to pot. Add peas and cook only 5 minutes longer.

Add dumplings. To make dumplings: Mix baking mix and milk until a soft dough forms. Drop by tablespoonfuls onto boiling stew. Simmer covered for 10 minutes, then uncover and simmer an additional 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Dumplings with Vegetables
raw_recipe.description: This creamy chicken and dumplings dish with vegetables is topped with biscuit dough dumplings for a hearty and comforting dish on a cold night.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is hands down the BEST ever! I'm not much of a cook, but when I made this my fiance called me "The Chicken & Dumpling Queen". We like ours nice and thick, so I used 3 cans of the Cream of Chicken Soup, 3 cups of chicken broth, and cut the veggies into small pieces. I made my own dumplings because I don't like the box stuff.
Take 1 3/4 cups of all purpose flour, 1/2 tspn baking soda, salt,3 tablespoons of veg. shortening, and 3/4 cups of low-fat buttermilk. Add all ingredients, stir til you get the consistency of dough. roll out dough and cut into 2 inch rectangles. Add to boiling stew and simmer for 10-15 minutes. It's really good on a cold night. It Rocks!!! Thanks Claire..I couldn't have impressed my fiance without your recipe!

I absolutely love this recipe. I play around with which veggies to add and sometimes omit the potatoes. I used leftover chicken from one I roasted (do not season the broth or it will be too salty), but I've also done a rotisserie chicken. I also hate the boring wet flour "biscuits" that every chicken and dumpling recipe ever calls for. I get the Pilsbury grands flaky biscuits (honey butter is my favorite) and quarter them and throw them in towards the end until cooked through. I also do chicken broth instead of water and usually have to double the broth ingredients.

Very good. I used extra thin chicken breasts, but doubled the amount. They shredded much easier. I doubled the poultry seasoning and pepper. I also made my own biscuits- 3cups flour, 4.5 tsp baking soda, 1.5 tsp salt, 4.5 tsb shortening, 2cups buttermilk. Great fall meal!

This is my second time making this dish. I made some modifications based on my first (failed) attempt and some comments from previous reviews. 

First, I didn't have celery, since I live in Turkey and it's hard to find here, but I didn't miss it a bit. We don't have Bisquick here either, but dumpling dough is so simple to make.

Second, I used chicken legs and thighs, which were cheaper and more flavorful than boneless skinless chicken breasts. They are quite easy to de-bone after cooking for that long.

Third, I left out the potatoes this time around; last time I found them bulky and flavorless, and there were so many of them there wasn't room for the dumplings! 

Finally, I added two chicken boullion cubes and left out the pre-made soup. I didn't have poultry seasoning either, so to spice up the dish, I added 1 tbsp of dried rosemary, 2 bay leaves, 1/2 tsp of cumin, and 2 cloves of garlic. 

With these modifications, it was the best chicken and dumplings I've ever eaten (not to brag ;)).

I made this tonight and it is a great starter. Of course I made a few changes (I always do). I used chicken broth instead of water and increased it to 4 cups. Did not have frozen peas so used frozen mixed vegetables. I cut the chicken up and sautéed it in olive oil. Then added the celery and garlic and onions cut up to the same pan. Then I added the seasonings listed plus many of my favorites. When all was browned I added it the pot that I had simmering with broth potatoes and carrots. I will definitely only use half the dumpling mix next time and am willing to try the recipe for homemade ones another poster listed. All in all a nice recipe. Much quicker than my “boil the whole chicken all day recipe” I normally make.

Absolutely perfect after a few small tweaks! My boyfriend is quite picky but even he called this a masterpiece! This will be my go-to chicken and dumpling recipe for years to come. 
My changes: 
-Doubled the water to 6 cups. It still turned out thick and creamy. 
-Didn't use onions due to my boyfriend's pickiness. I personally love them but this was delicious even without. 
-Raised temperature to medium-low for the long simmer. 
-Used three potatoes instead of four, diced rather than quartered. I didn't fancy the idea of a stew with large chunks of potato. 
-Once I added the peas, I raised the temperature to med-high in order to bring to a boil. After the dumpling dough was added, I lowered it to med-low.

No doubt about it... awesome comfort food! I made this recipe twice. The 1st time I followed the recipe exactly and thought that it lacked a little depth in the taste. Also the dumplings absorbed too much of the broth in the cool down. So there was enough broth for the first night, but the on the next night for the leftovers, I added Chicken stock to the stew. The 2nd time I made this recipe, I used Chicken stock instead of the water. That gave the dish a more robust flavor, and I cut the amount of dumplings in half and the remedied the absorption of the broth issue. Overall its like I said earlier, Awesome comfort food!

Wow! Delicious! I added chicken broth base and about 3 cups more water to the recipe because I like a lot of soup. I like to add the powered broth base so I can make it richer. I cut up the chicken and threw everything in the pot together. I let it come to a boil and then cooked it on low for about 30 minutes more before adding the dumplings. I thickened the stew with a few teaspoons of corn starch before I added the dumplings. One of my favorite recipes and a lot like the one my dad use to make.

We absolutely loved this recipe! It's my new "go to" for chicken and dumplings! I diced the onion and celery and sauteed them in a bit of butter, and I used a 32oz box of chicken stock instead of water. Just delicious, thank you for sharing your recipe!
The stew turned out delicious! However I did some steps differently. 1. I used Grands canned biscuits instead of making them from scratch.

I used another receipt for the dumplings. I also seasoned my dumplings. It was great.

Dumpling recipe:
To Make Dumplings: In a medium bowl, stir together the flour, baking powder and salt. In a small bowl, mix together 1/2 cup of milk and 2 tablespoons of oil. Pour into the dry ingredients, stirring just until moistened.

I made this as directed except I used cut green beans in place of the peas and large canned biscuits cut into quarters for the dumplings. I topped with parsley and a bit of paprika. Mmmmm. Oh yes, I almost forgot ... I also used my crockpot.
I added extra poultry seasoning. I will definitely make again.

My husband raved. I typically make homemade meals and he often says they're really good (genuinely) but he raved and raved about this! He had 3 helpings! I did make some changes: I doubled the recipe. I used 2 cans cream of chicken and 2 cans cream of mushroom. And I used homemade chicken bone broth from the bones of 2 rotisserie chickens and used 8cups of that instead of water. Instead of 6cups water. I used the rotisserie chicken meat (from Sam's). I skipped the peas because I didn't have any. I put in a cup of celery and 10 carrots, sliced. And a diy poultry seasoning (rosemary, sage, margoram, thyme & paprika). I let it all simmer in a crockpot for 4 hours then made cheddar bag biscuit dough according to the box, using white cheddar. And made those the dumplings. 100% will make again!!!
This is a chosen birthday dinner for my husband every year. This is the best iteration of Chicken and Dumplings we've had.

This is STILL our family's go-to for chicken and dumplings. I can't believe I have to dig for it now! It's great on its own, but a few minor tweaks take this to really good to truly great. 1: Use herbs de provence. Can be in addition or in place of poultry seasoning. 2: Use fresh garlic at the initial saute phase. Everything is better with garlic. Either just smash it or you can mince it, as a texture preference. 3: Make your own baking mix. For this recipe cut together 3 cups flour, 4 1/2 tsp baking powder, 3/4 tsp salt, 3 tsp COLD butter. Use as normal.

Well I think this recipe is wonderful, but I needed a little more water, so I added a cup of chicken broth. I forgot to put my chicken and peas in before my dumplings which created a problem-- when I tried to gently fold them in my dumplings disintegrated into a mush. My fault. This has to be done in the exact order to avoid that.
it came out fabulous. emptied the pot the first night.
Loved it! Used canned biscuits instead of making them from scratch to save some time. It was great!
